name: Sassafras 16-Strand Climbing Rope
title: Sassafras 16 Strand Climbing Rope for Arborists
meta: Sassafras is a classic 16 strand climbing rope for hitch climbing on MRS. See how it handles, which hitches suit it, and what it typically costs.
tagline: A traditional 16-strand arborist climbing line for friction-hitch work.
summary: Sassafras is a traditional 16 strand climbing rope built for arborists who still climb on a doubled line with a friction hitch. It has the firm, round feel 16-strand fans like and holds a hitch predictably once it is broken in.
highlights: Classic 16-strand braided construction
Firm, round hand that grips a friction hitch well
Suited to moving rope system (MRS) climbing
Good choice for climbers learning hitch work
Sold in common arborist lengths

p: Sixteen-strand rope has been the standard arborist climbing line for decades, and Sassafras keeps that feel. The cover is tight and the rope stays round under load, so a Blake's, Distel, or VT hitch grabs and releases the same way every time. Expect a stiffer hand for the first few climbs; it softens with use.

On a doubled-rope (MRS) system it works well with a friction saver or a ring-and-ring cambium saver, and it runs cleanly through a micro pulley on your hitch. It is not a low-stretch kernmantle, so it has a little more give on a long limb walk than a 24-strand line.

Sixteen-strand lines are also easy to splice and inspect. The braid pattern shows damage clearly, so cuts, pulled strands, and fuzzed sections are easy to spot when you run the rope through your hands before a climb.

Match your hitch cord to the rope diameter and test the hitch low before you commit to height. Keep the rope out of chips and sap, store it in a rope bag away from sunlight and fuel, and retire it after cuts, glazing, or crushed sections.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Is 16-strand rope still good for climbing?
faq.a: Yes. Many climbers prefer 16-strand for MRS hitch climbing because it holds a friction hitch consistently and is easy to splice or tie off.

faq.q: Can I use Sassafras on SRS?
faq.a: Check the manufacturer's instructions and your device's approved rope list first. Many SRS devices are designed around 11–13 mm kernmantle or 24-strand ropes.

name: Courant Kalimba Bubblegum 11.9 mm Climbing Rope
title: Courant Kalimba Bubble Gum Rope 11.9 mm Climbing Line
h1: Courant Kalimba Bubble Gum Rope, 11.9 mm
meta: Courant Kalimba in Bubblegum: the bubble gum rope climbers spot from the ground. An 11.9 mm 24-strand line for MRS and SRS. Specs, care, and typical price.
tagline: A supple 11.9 mm 24-strand climbing line in a high-visibility pink colorway.
summary: The Courant Kalimba in Bubblegum is the bubble gum rope a lot of climbers ask for by color: an 11.9 mm, 24-strand arborist line that is easy to see in the canopy. It handles well on both doubled-rope and single-rope systems and runs smoothly through most modern hardware.
highlights: 11.9 mm 24-strand construction
Bright Bubblegum pink color stands out in the canopy and on the ground
Works on MRS and SRS setups within device rope ranges
Supple hand that ties knots and hitches easily
Low-stretch feel for efficient ascents

p: Kalimba is Courant's mid-diameter climbing line, and at 11.9 mm it sits right in the range most mechanical devices, rope wrenches, and friction hitches are built around. The 24-strand cover gives a smooth, round profile that feeds through a hitch or a device without catching, and it stays manageable when you are tending slack on a long limb walk.

The Bubblegum colorway is more than a style choice. A bright line is easier for your ground person to track, easier to spot when you are setting a canopy anchor, and much easier to keep separate from a rigging line or a second climbing line in the same tree.

Kalimba is also a good size for climbers who want one rope to cover both systems. At 11.9 mm it is thick enough to feel secure in the hand on a doubled line, yet not so bulky that it drags through an SRS device or wears you out on a long footlock or ascent.

On a doubled-rope system, Kalimba holds a Distel or VT hitch well with a matching hitch cord, and it tends a micro pulley cleanly. On a stationary rope system it pairs with devices such as the ISC Rope Wrench or a mechanical SRS device, as long as the device maker lists 11.9 mm in its approved range.

For removals where you are climbing and cutting all day, the low-stretch feel means less bounce on ascents and more direct control on descents. Keep it away from the saw and treat it as a climbing-only line; never use your climbing rope for rigging.

On pruning climbs the supple hand pays off. The rope ties a tight bowline or anchor hitch, unties easily after a heavy day, and coils without fighting you. It also packs into a standard rope bag with room to spare in 150 ft lengths.
Kalimba also makes a good rope for teaching. The bright color helps an instructor on the ground follow what a student's system is doing at every point in the climb.

Coil or bag the rope at the end of the day, keep it out of fuel, bar oil, and direct sun, and wash it only as the manufacturer allows. Run the full length through your hands before each climb, feeling for flat spots, glazing, core damage, or cuts in the cover.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire the rope if you find damage or if it has taken a significant shock load.

Write the date the rope went into service on a tag or in your gear log, and track climbing hours if your employer requires it. Rotate rope ends from time to time so wear spreads along the length instead of building up at one end.

faq.q: What is bubble gum rope?
faq.a: Climbers use the name for Courant Kalimba in its Bubblegum pink colorway. It is the same 11.9 mm 24-strand climbing line as other Kalimba colors.

faq.q: Will Kalimba work with my SRS device?
faq.a: Most devices built for 11–13 mm ropes accept 11.9 mm, but always confirm the rope is on the device maker's approved list.

faq.q: Should I get 150 or 200 feet?
faq.a: 150 ft covers most residential trees on a doubled system. Choose 200 ft for tall trees, long SRS descents, or when you want spare length to cut off worn ends.

name: Yale Poison Moon 11.7 mm Climbing Rope
title: Yale Poison Moon 11.7 mm: Poison Ivy Rope in a New Color
h1: Yale Poison Moon 11.7 mm, a Poison Ivy Rope Colorway
meta: Yale Poison Moon is a colorway of the popular Poison Ivy rope: an 11.7 mm 24-strand climbing line for MRS and SRS. Handling, hardware fit, and price.
tagline: Yale's 11.7 mm 24-strand climbing line in the Poison Moon colorway.
summary: Yale Poison Moon is built on the same 11.7 mm, 24-strand design as the well-known Poison Ivy rope, in a different colorway. It is a light, supple line that runs smoothly through friction hitches and mechanical devices on both moving and stationary rope systems.
highlights: 11.7 mm diameter fits most hitch cords and SRS devices
24-strand cover for a smooth, round profile
Light and supple, easy to coil and throw
Distinct colorway helps separate climbing and rigging lines
From Yale Cordage, a long-time arborist rope maker

p: Poison Ivy earned its following because it is light in the hand, stays round, and works with almost any hitch or device a climber is likely to own. Poison Moon uses that same 11.7 mm, 24-strand design, so the handling is what Poison Ivy users already know. The change is the color, which helps when a crew runs several climbing lines and wants each one easy to identify.
At 11.7 mm, the rope sits in the middle of the common 11–13 mm range. That makes it easy to pair with a split-tail and pulley on MRS, or with a rope wrench or mechanical device on SRS.

Yale has made arborist rope for a long time, and its climbing lines are widely used by tree crews across the US. That track record matters with life-support rope, where consistency from one production run to the next is part of what you are paying for. Poison Moon gives you that consistency with a look that is easy to tell apart on a crowded job.

body.h: How it handles in the tree
p: The low-stretch build gives efficient ascents and a direct feel when you are moving laterally. Hitches set and release cleanly, and the smooth cover is easy on friction savers and cambium savers. The lighter weight is noticeable on long SRS lines and on big removals where you carry a lot of rope.

Like any thinner, slicker line, it can run a little faster through some hitches than a thicker 16-strand. Test your hitch and adjust wraps or braids low in the tree before climbing high. Pair it with a Petzl Zigzag or similar only if the rope is within the device's listed range.

On SRS the lighter weight is a real advantage. A long single line from a canopy anchor to the ground can be heavy to haul up for a basal tie or to drag around the tree. A thinner, lighter line makes those resets less tiring. On MRS, the smooth cover helps a micro pulley tend the hitch without hanging up.
For a crew that standardizes on Poison Ivy, adding Poison Moon lets each climber have a distinct line while keeping hitch cords and devices the same across the crew.
Check the full length before each climb for cover cuts, stiff or flattened sections, glazing from heat, and chemical contamination. Keep it in a bag and away from saw fuel, bar oil, and battery acid.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

If you work around sap-heavy species such as pine, clean sap off promptly; it stiffens the cover and changes how hitches grip. Store the rope loose in a bag rather than tightly coiled for long periods, and keep a record of when it went into service.

faq.q: Is Poison Moon the same rope as Poison Ivy?
faq.a: It uses the same 11.7 mm 24-strand design. The main difference is the colorway.

faq.q: Is 11.7 mm too thin for a hitch climb?
faq.a: No, it is a common climbing diameter. Choose a hitch cord the maker approves for that rope size and test the hitch before you climb.

faq.q: Can I rig with it?
faq.a: No. Keep climbing rope for climbing only and use a dedicated rigging line for lowering wood.

name: Notch Magneato Rope Runner Tether
title: Notch Magneato Tether for the Rope Runner
meta: The Notch Magneato tether keeps a Rope Runner or similar device attached and within reach on your saddle. How it works, where it fits, and price.
tagline: A magnetic-catch tether that keeps your rope runner tidy and close at hand.
summary: The Notch Magneato is a short tether with a magnetic catch that keeps a Rope Runner or similar device organized on your saddle. It reduces fumbling when you switch between ascending, working, and descending.
highlights: Magnetic catch for quick, one-handed clipping
Keeps the device close and oriented
Helps prevent dropped or misplaced hardware
Accessory only, not a life-support connector
specs: Notch Rope Runner (check fit for other devices)

p: When you climb on a mechanical device, small handling details add up: where the device rides, how you grab it, and how quickly you can get it back in position after you unclip. The Magneato gives the device a consistent parking spot with a magnetic catch, so you can find it by feel and keep it from flopping around while you work.
It is an organizing accessory. It does not replace your bridge, your connecting carabiner, or any part of your life-support system.

Climbers who work all day on SRS tend to set up their saddle the same way every time so their hands go to the right spot without looking. A magnetic catch supports that habit: the device lands in the same place each time you park it, and you can grab it with a gloved hand while your other hand holds the saw or the rope.

Check fit with your saddle and device, and make sure the tether cannot interfere with your hitch, device cam, or carabiner gate. Look over the carabiners and hardware in our carabiners and hardware section for life-support connectors.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.
Keep the magnetic catch clean of metal filings and grit, and check that the tether material and stitching are in good shape.

faq.q: Is the Magneato rated for life support?
faq.a: No. Treat it as a gear-organizing accessory and never load it as part of your climbing system.

faq.q: Does it only work with the Rope Runner?
faq.a: It is designed around the Rope Runner. Check fit before using it with other devices.

name: 1/2 in Whoopie Sling
title: 1/2 in Whoopie Slings for Arborist Rigging
meta: Half-inch whoopie slings give arborists an adjustable, lightweight anchor for rigging blocks and lowering devices. How they work, sizing, and price.
tagline: Adjustable synthetic sling for setting rigging anchors fast.
summary: Whoopie slings are adjustable synthetic slings that let you set a rigging block or lowering anchor at the right height and tension without tying knots. This 1/2 in version is a common size for residential removal and pruning rigging.
highlights: Adjustable length for different stem and limb diameters
Fixed eye plus adjustable eye
Lightweight 12-strand synthetic construction
No knots to untie after a heavy load
Pairs with blocks, rings, and lowering devices
specs: One fixed eye, one adjustable eye

p: A whoopie sling is a spliced 12-strand sling with a long buried tail, so the adjustable eye can grow or shrink to fit the stem. Choke it around the spar, snug it down, and hang your block exactly where you want it. After the load comes off, it slides back open, which saves a lot of time over picking out a tight knot.
Because the high-modulus fiber stretches very little, the anchor stays where you set it. That also means it is not a shock absorber, so plan cuts and rigging forces carefully.

Choose a length that wraps the stems you usually rig on with room to choke, and always use the sling within the working load limit the manufacturer specifies. Avoid sharp edges, keep it away from the saw, and inspect the splices and the adjustable section for pulled strands, melting, or abrasion before each use.
Pair it with a rigging block or other adjustable slings rated for the loads you will be catching. Rigging should be planned by trained workers following ANSI Z133.
Carry two or three lengths in the rigging bag. A short sling covers small spars and limbs, and a longer one reaches around big leaders or a pair of stems when you need a wider anchor.

faq.q: Can a whoopie sling slip under load?
faq.a: When set up correctly the bury locks the adjustable eye under load. Follow the maker's instructions for minimum bury and setup.

faq.q: What is the working load limit?
faq.a: It depends on the specific rope and splice. Use the rating on the tag or the maker's data, not the rope's breaking strength.

name: Husqvarna D-Shaped Carabiner
title: Husqvarna D Shape Carabiner, Auto-Locking
meta: A Husqvarna D shape carabiner with an auto-locking gate for arborist kits. Where D-shapes fit in your system, how to check one, and typical price.
tagline: Auto-locking D-shaped carabiner for arborist climbing kits.
summary: This Husqvarna D shape carabiner has an auto-locking gate and the asymmetric profile that keeps loads near the strong spine. It is a practical connector for lanyards, friction savers, and general climbing hardware.
highlights: D shape keeps the load near the spine
Auto-locking gate closes and locks on its own
Aluminum body keeps weight down
Good everyday connector for an arborist kit

p: A D-shaped carabiner pushes the load toward the spine, which is the strongest part of the carabiner. That makes it a good choice where loading is predictable: on a lanyard end, a friction saver ring, or a pulley. An auto-locking gate means you do not have to remember to screw it shut after every clip.
For devices that can twist or shift, such as some hitch setups, consider an oval or pear shape instead so the carabiner stays seated.

Husqvarna sells a range of climbing hardware alongside its saws, and this D-shape is meant as a general connector for the gear bag. Having a few matching carabiners makes it easier to standardize your kit so everything on the saddle works the same way.

Confirm the strength markings and any certification on the spine meet your requirements for life support. Check that the gate opens, closes, and locks fully without sticking, and keep it clean of sap and grit. Retire carabiners that have been dropped from height or show cracks, sharp edges, or worn grooves.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Browse more auto-locking carabiners.
Keep carabiners used for life support separate from those used for gear and rigging.

faq.q: Is a D shape better than an oval carabiner?
faq.a: A D-shape is stronger along the spine for predictable loads. Ovals keep devices centered and are better for some pulley and rope-grab setups.

faq.q: Can I use it for climbing?
faq.a: Only if its markings and certification meet the standard required for your life-support system. Check the spine before use.

name: Husqvarna Power Axe 350i Battery Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna Power Axe 350i Chainsaw: Battery Kit Guide
h1: Husqvarna Power Axe 350i Chainsaw, Battery Kit
meta: The Husqvarna Power Axe 350i chainsaw is a 40V battery rear-handle saw for ground work and cleanup. Kit contents, bar options, runtime tips, and price.
tagline: A 40V battery rear-handle saw for ground crews, cleanup, and storm limbing.
summary: The Husqvarna Power Axe 350i chainsaw is a battery-powered rear-handle saw built for limbing, bucking small wood, and cleanup on the ground. It starts at the push of a trigger, runs quiet, and needs no fuel mixing, which makes it a handy second saw on a tree crew.
highlights: 40V-class Husqvarna battery platform
Brushless motor with instant start
Rear-handle design for ground work
Much quieter than a gas saw, no fuel mix
Kit includes battery and charger

body.h: Where the 350i fits on a tree crew
p: Most crews already run a gas saw for felling and heavy bucking. The Power Axe 350i is for everything around that work: limbing brush at the chipper, cutting small stems to length, clearing storm debris along a driveway, and cleanup cuts where starting a gas saw over and over wastes time. Pull the trigger and it runs, release and it stops, so there is no idling saw sitting on the stump.

Low noise matters on residential jobs. The 350i lets the ground crew work early in the morning or near occupied buildings with less disruption, and makes communication between climber and ground easier while the saw is running.

For a homeowner with a big property or a landscape crew that handles small trees, the 350i can also be the main saw. It handles blowdowns, firewood-size wood, and small removals without the noise or the fuel can.

The brushless motor delivers steady chain speed for wood in the range a 16 in bar handles comfortably. It is not a replacement for a 60 cc gas saw in big hardwood, but it handles brush, firewood-size rounds, and limbing with good feed. Keep the chain sharp; a dull chain drains a battery much faster than a sharp one.

Runtime depends on the battery size, wood, and how hard you cut. Many users carry a second battery and swap while the first charges in the truck. Batteries are shared across Husqvarna's 40V-class battery tools, so the same packs can run a blower or trimmer from the same line.

The kit typically ships with a 16 in bar and chain, a battery, and a charger. That makes it ready to work out of the box, and a good starting point if you are building into Husqvarna's battery platform. Some users later add the bare tool version of other Husqvarna battery tools to make use of the same packs.

Check chain tension and bar oil at every battery swap. Clean chips from the sprocket cover and motor vents, and file or replace the chain when it starts to throw dust instead of chips. Store batteries in a cool, dry place and do not leave them in a hot cab all day.

A battery saw cuts just as hard as a gas saw. Wear chainsaw-rated chaps or pants, eye and hearing protection, gloves, and a helmet, and keep two hands on the saw. Remove the battery before clearing jams or changing the chain. Browse more battery-powered equipment to build out a platform.
Battery saws still need the same care as gas saws in the cut. Watch for pinching, plan your relief cuts, and avoid the upper quadrant of the bar nose where kickback starts.
Inspect the chain catcher and chain brake regularly, and replace a worn drive sprocket when you notice the chain riding poorly. Keep the battery contacts clean and dry.

faq.q: Does the Husqvarna Power Axe 350i kit include a battery?
faq.a: The kit version includes a battery and charger. The bare-tool version does not, so check the listing before buying.

faq.q: Can the 350i replace my gas saw?
faq.a: For limbing, brush, and small bucking it can. For felling and large-diameter hardwood, most crews still use a gas saw.

faq.q: Which batteries work with it?
faq.a: It runs on Husqvarna's 40V-class battery line, the same packs used by their other battery tools in that range.

name: Husqvarna T542i XP Top-Handle Battery Chainsaw Kit
title: Husqvarna 542i XP Top-Handle Battery Chainsaw Kit
h1: Husqvarna 542i XP Top-Handle Battery Chainsaw Kit (T542i XP)
meta: The Husqvarna 542i XP (T542i XP) is a pro top-handle battery chainsaw for in-tree work. Kit contents, bar options, how it compares to gas, and price.
tagline: Professional battery top-handle saw for climbers working in the canopy.
summary: The Husqvarna 542i XP, sold as the T542i XP, is a professional top-handle battery chainsaw built for climbers who prune and remove in the canopy. It is light, quiet, and starts instantly, so you can make a cut, hang it on your saddle, and move on without restarting a gas saw.
highlights: Top-handle design for trained arborists working in the tree
Runs on Husqvarna's 36V/40V-class professional batteries
Instant start, no idle between cuts
Lanyard ring for tethering to the saddle
Kit includes battery and charger

p: The T542i XP is aimed at professional climbers. The compact top-handle layout keeps the saw balanced when you are working from a lanyard, and the low weight reduces fatigue on long pruning days. Because a battery saw does not idle, you can cut, let go of the trigger, and clip it back to your saddle without the saw running against your leg.
Quiet operation helps on residential work and with communication. You can hear your ground crew call out and talk through rigging cuts while the saw is in your hand, without stopping it first.

The saw ships as a kit with a battery and charger, so it is ready to climb with once the bar is oiled and the chain is tensioned. A lanyard ring lets you hang it from a saw lanyard on your saddle the same way you would a gas top-handle.

A good gas top-handle still has the edge in endurance on all-day removals in big wood. For pruning, crown reductions, and small-to-medium removals, the 542i XP keeps up and removes the hassle of starting a hot saw on a rope, mixing fuel, and dealing with fumes in your face.

Plan your battery supply around the job. One battery may cover a light pruning climb; a removal will usually call for a spare. Keep the chain sharp and correctly tensioned, since a dull chain cuts runtime noticeably.

Batteries share Husqvarna's professional battery platform, so a crew that already runs Husqvarna battery blowers or pole saws can use the same packs across the gear. Keep spare packs charged in the truck and rotate them through the day. Cold weather shortens runtime, so keep batteries in the cab until you need them.

On many crews the battery top-handle has become the default pruning saw, with a gas top-handle kept for heavy removals. That split lets the climber pick the right tool for the day without giving up the convenience of instant start on most jobs.

Top-handle saws are designed for trained arborists working in trees. ANSI Z133 requires a top-handle saw to be operated with two hands except in limited circumstances, and only by trained users. Do not use it on the ground in place of a rear-handle saw.

Tether the saw with a chainsaw lanyard, wear a climbing helmet with eye and hearing protection, and keep your climbing line and lanyard out of the cutting path. Remove the battery before servicing the chain or clearing debris.
Inspect the chain brake, chain catcher, and throttle lockout before every climb, and do not modify or bypass them.
Keep the chain sharp and the bar oiled. A dull chain on a top-handle saw encourages pushing and awkward body positions, which is exactly what you want to avoid in the tree.

faq.q: Is the Husqvarna 542i XP the same as the T542i XP?
faq.a: Yes. People search for it both ways; T542i XP is Husqvarna's model name for the top-handle battery saw.

faq.q: What bar length should I run?
faq.a: A 12 in bar suits pruning and light work. A 14 in bar gives more reach for removals. Use only bar and chain combinations Husqvarna lists for the saw.

faq.q: Can I use a top-handle saw on the ground?
faq.a: Top-handle saws are made for use in the tree by trained arborists. On the ground, use a rear-handle saw.

name: Notch 13 in Tri-Edge Saw Blade
title: Notch Blade: 13 in Tri-Edge Replacement Saw Blade
meta: This Notch blade is a 13 in tri-edge replacement pruning saw blade with aggressive pull-cut teeth for green wood. Fit, uses, care, and typical price.
tagline: Replacement 13 in tri-edge pruning blade for green wood.
summary: This Notch blade is a 13 in tri-edge pruning saw blade made for fast cutting in green wood. It is a replacement blade, so you can swap in a fresh edge instead of buying a whole new saw.
highlights: 13 in blade length
Tri-edge teeth cut on the pull stroke
Built for green wood pruning
Replace the blade, keep the handle

p: A 13 in blade is a good middle size for climbers and ground workers: long enough to clear limbs a few inches thick, short enough to handle in tight crowns. The tri-edge teeth cut on the pull stroke, which keeps the blade straight and gives clean, quick cuts in live wood.
Use it for pruning cuts where a chainsaw is overkill or too risky, such as near the trunk collar or close to your rope.

Tri-edge teeth have three cutting faces per tooth, which clears sawdust quickly and keeps the blade from binding in wet, fibrous wood. That makes the blade a good fit for summer pruning when the wood is full of sap.

Confirm the blade matches your Notch saw handle or scabbard before ordering. Wipe sap off after use, keep it dry, and store it in a scabbard. Impulse-hardened teeth are not meant to be filed, so replace the blade when it starts to drag. Find more options under replacement blades.

Swap blades with the saw in a safe position on the ground, not in the tree, and confirm the blade is locked in before climbing. Keep a spare blade in the truck so a dull or bent blade does not slow down a pruning job.

faq.q: Can I sharpen a tri-edge blade?
faq.a: Hardened tri-edge teeth are generally not filed. Replace the blade when it dulls.

faq.q: Will it fit other brands' handles?
faq.a: Check the mounting pattern. It is meant for compatible Notch handles.

name: Husqvarna 330LK String Trimmer
title: Husqvarna 330LK Trimmer: Specs, Attachments & Price
meta: The Husqvarna 330LK is a pro split-shaft string trimmer that takes combi attachments. See which attachments fit, where it works best, and typical price.
tagline: A pro split-shaft trimmer that doubles as a combi power head.
summary: The Husqvarna 330LK is a professional gas string trimmer with a detachable shaft, so the same power head can run trimmer, edger, and pole saw attachments. For tree and landscape crews it is one engine that covers a lot of jobsite cleanup.
highlights: Split-shaft combi design accepts Husqvarna attachments
Loop handle for good control in tight spots
Commercial-grade 2-stroke engine
Easy transport with the shaft separated
Good fit for crews who want one power head

p: The LK in 330LK means loop handle and combi shaft. Pull the lower shaft and you can swap the trimmer head for other Husqvarna combi attachments, such as an edger, hedge trimmer, or pole saw. On a tree crew, that means one power head in the truck can trim around a stump site, edge a bed after a removal, and take small limbs off a low branch with a pole saw attachment.
The split shaft also makes the unit easier to store and transport. It fits in a truck box or trailer rack that would not take a full-length straight-shaft trimmer.

The 330LK is the more powerful of Husqvarna's two common combi units. That extra power helps when you run heavier attachments, such as a pole saw in hardwood or a brushcutter blade in thick growth, where a lighter engine can bog. Searches for 330LK Husqvarna and Husqvarna 330LK weed eater point to the same machine.

Husqvarna attachments in its combi line share the same coupling, so check the attachment's compatibility list before buying. The most common add-ons for tree work are the pole saw for limbing and clearance, and the edger for cleanup around hardscape after stump grinding. Brushcutter blades, where approved, help clear heavy weeds and saplings on overgrown sites.
Add attachments one at a time as the work calls for them. The point of a combi system is to cover more jobs without buying separate engines, not to carry every attachment on every job.

A pole saw attachment on a gas power head is a good fit for clearance pruning along driveways and sidewalks, where you can reach limbs from the ground without a climber. Keep in mind that a pole saw on a combi unit adds weight at the end of a long shaft, so take breaks and keep a good stance. Never use a pole saw near power lines; follow ANSI Z133 approach distances.

Use fresh fuel mixed at the ratio in the operator's manual, and drain or stabilize fuel if the unit will sit. Clean the air filter regularly on dusty jobs, check the spark plug at the start of the season, and keep the shaft coupling clean so attachments seat fully.

Wear eye protection, hearing protection, long pants, and sturdy boots. Keep bystanders well back, since a trimmer throws debris farther than most people expect. Compare it with the Husqvarna 525LK if you want a lighter combi unit.

At the end of the day, clean grass and debris from the trimmer head, the guard, and the engine cooling fins. Check the gearhead grease at the intervals in the manual and tighten any loose fasteners. A few minutes of care keeps the unit starting easily and running at full power.

faq.q: What attachments fit the Husqvarna 330LK?
faq.a: It takes attachments from Husqvarna's combi system, such as edger, hedge trimmer, and pole saw heads. Confirm compatibility on the attachment listing.

faq.q: Is the 330LK a 2-stroke?
faq.a: Yes. It runs on gas mixed with 2-stroke oil at the ratio in the manual.

faq.q: Is it heavier than the 525LK?
faq.a: The 330LK is the larger, more powerful unit. The 525LK is lighter and easier to carry all day.

name: Husqvarna 525L Gas String Trimmer
title: Husqvarna 525L Gas String Trimmer: Specs & Price
meta: The Husqvarna 525L is a light, commercial 25.4 cc gas string trimmer for cleanup around tree jobs. Specs, who it suits, upkeep tips, and typical price.
tagline: Light commercial straight-shaft trimmer for jobsite cleanup.
summary: The Husqvarna 525L is a lightweight commercial gas string trimmer with a 25.4 cc engine, a straight shaft, and a loop handle. It is easy to carry all day and gives tree and landscape crews dependable trimming for site cleanup.
highlights: 25.4 cc X-Torq 2-stroke engine
Straight shaft for reach under shrubs and fences
Loop handle for control in tight spaces
Light enough for all-day use
Commercial-grade build

p: The 525L sits in the sweet spot for commercial trimmers: enough power to cut through heavy grass and weeds, but light enough that one person can run it for hours. The X-Torq engine is designed for lower emissions and better fuel economy than older 2-stroke designs, which you will notice over a long season.

The one-piece straight shaft reaches under hedges, along fence lines, and around stumps better than a curved shaft. The loop handle keeps the unit nimble when you are working around landscape beds and obstacles.

Searches for 525L Husqvarna and Husqvarna 525L weed eater lead to the same machine. It has a reputation for starting easily and running for years with basic maintenance, which is why it is common in commercial landscape trailers as well as on tree crews.

After a removal or stump grind, there is always cleanup: trimming back grass the equipment flattened, clearing weeds where the chipper sat, and tidying the edges of the work zone. The 525L handles that work quickly and keeps the site looking finished when the customer walks out.
If you want attachments too, look at the Husqvarna 525LK, which has the same engine size with a split combi shaft.

Trimmer work around tree jobs also includes clearing access. Before a crew sets up on an overgrown lot, a quick pass with a trimmer around the base of the tree and along the path for the chipper hose makes it easier to see trip hazards, roots, and debris. The 525L is light enough that a ground worker can do that clearing without getting worn out before the real work starts.

The straight shaft also helps around hardscape and steps. You can tilt the head to trim along a curb or under a bench without stooping, and the head stays stable on the ground for edging-style passes.
The Husqvarna 525L trimmer price usually lands in the high 300s from US dealers and retailers. That is more than a homeowner trimmer, but it is built to run every day and be serviced, not replaced.

Use fresh mixed fuel, clean the air filter often, and replace the spark plug and fuel filter as the manual recommends. Wear eye and hearing protection, long pants, and boots, and keep others clear of the cutting area.

The 525LS is a related model with a different handle and shaft configuration. If you are comparing, check the operator manuals for each so you know what you are getting. For most tree crews, the 525L is the simpler, all-round choice.

Store the unit with an empty tank or stabilized fuel over the winter, and check the trimmer head for wear before the season starts. Replace worn eyelets so the line does not cut through the head housing.

faq.q: What is the Husqvarna 525L trimmer price?
faq.a: A typical US street price is in the high 300s. Prices vary by dealer and promotions.

faq.q: What is the difference between the 525L and 525LK?
faq.a: Both use a 25.4 cc engine. The 525L has a one-piece straight shaft; the 525LK has a split shaft that accepts combi attachments.

faq.q: Is the 525L good for weed eating around stumps?
faq.a: Yes. It has the power for heavy weeds and the reach to trim around stumps and roots.

name: Husqvarna 525LK Combination Trimmer
title: Husqvarna 525LK Combi Trimmer: Husqvarna 525 Guide
meta: The Husqvarna 525LK is the split-shaft version of the Husqvarna 525 trimmer: 25.4 cc, light, and ready for combi attachments. Specs, uses, and price.
tagline: Light 25.4 cc combi power head with a trimmer attachment.
summary: The Husqvarna 525LK is the split-shaft combi version of the Husqvarna 525 trimmer, pairing a light 25.4 cc engine with a coupling that accepts other combi attachments. Crews get a commercial string trimmer that can also run an edger, hedge trimmer, or pole saw.
highlights: 25.4 cc X-Torq 2-stroke engine
Split shaft accepts Husqvarna combi attachments
Light, balanced power head for all-day use
Loop handle for control
Breaks down for compact transport

p: Husqvarna's 525 series covers a group of light commercial trimmers built around the same 25.4 cc engine. The 525L has a fixed straight shaft, and the 525LK adds a split shaft so the lower half can be swapped for other attachments. If you are looking for a Husqvarna 525 weed eater that can do more than trim, the LK is the one to look at.
The engine is light enough to carry for long stretches without wearing you out, yet strong enough for heavy grass and weeds around a job site.

The combi coupling is quick to use. Loosen the knob, press the release, and slide the attachment out; slide the next one in until it locks, then tighten. There are no tools needed, so switching from trimming to edging takes less than a minute on site.
Searches for Husqvarna 525 and 525 Husqvarna usually land on one of these two models, so it pays to check which shaft you are getting before you order.

For tree crews, the pole saw attachment is the obvious add-on: it lets a ground worker clear low limbs, raise canopies over sidewalks, and cut small storm damage without pulling out a separate pole saw engine. An edger attachment cleans up hardscape after stump grinding, and a hedge trimmer attachment handles shrub work that often comes up on residential jobs.
Each attachment snaps onto the same coupling, so you carry one engine and several lightweight shafts. Check that each attachment is listed as compatible with the 525LK coupling before buying.

Combi units also simplify maintenance. You only have one engine to service, one air filter to clean, and one spark plug to replace, instead of a separate engine for every tool. That is a real saving for small crews and owner-operators.
Think about storage too. Attachments are easy to lose or damage loose in a truck bed. A simple rack or tube keeps them clean and protects the drive shafts and couplings.

Mix fuel fresh at the ratio in the manual and use it within a few weeks, or add stabilizer. Clean the air filter often on dusty jobs and keep the coupling free of grit so attachments seat and lock fully. Replace the trimmer line with the size Husqvarna recommends for the head.

Wear eye and hearing protection, long pants, and boots. When running a pole saw attachment, also wear a helmet and stay out from under the limb you are cutting. Compare it with the larger Husqvarna 330LK if you need more power.

Check the shaft coupling and the drive shaft splines from time to time. Worn or damaged splines cause slipping and vibration. Replace the trimmer head eyelets as they wear, and keep the cutting attachment guard in place; it limits how far debris is thrown and keeps line at the right length.

faq.q: Is the Husqvarna 525LK the same engine as the 525L?
faq.a: Yes, both use a 25.4 cc engine. The LK has a split combi shaft and the L has a one-piece shaft.

faq.q: Can I put a pole saw on a Husqvarna 525?
faq.a: On the 525LK, yes, with a compatible Husqvarna combi pole saw attachment. The 525L's fixed shaft does not take attachments.

faq.q: What line size does it use?
faq.a: Use the line diameter listed for the trimmer head in your operator's manual.

name: Husqvarna 590BTS Pro Backpack Blower
title: Husqvarna 590BTS Backpack Blower: Pro Cleanup Guide
meta: The Husqvarna 590BTS backpack blower is a high-output gas blower for clearing chips, sawdust, and leaves after tree work. Features, fit, and price.
tagline: High-output gas backpack blower for heavy cleanup after tree work.
summary: The Husqvarna 590BTS backpack blower is one of the most powerful gas backpack blowers in Husqvarna's professional range. Tree crews use it to clear chips, sawdust, and leaves from lawns, driveways, and roofs at the end of a job.
highlights: Top-of-range output in Husqvarna's backpack blowers
Tube-mounted throttle for one-hand control
Padded harness and back pad for all-day carry
Commercial 2-stroke engine
Built for heavy, wet debris and large areas

body.h: Why a big blower matters on tree jobs
p: Cleanup is what the customer remembers. After a removal, sawdust gets ground into the lawn, chips scatter across the driveway, and small twigs hide in landscape beds. A strong backpack blower moves all of that quickly, including damp sawdust and packed chips that a smaller handheld blower just pushes around.

The 590BTS sits at the top of Husqvarna's backpack blower range. That extra output pays off on big properties, wet fall leaves, and storm cleanup where you are moving a lot of material in a short time.

The blower also earns its keep on roofs and gutters after a crown cleaning or removal over a house. A strong blower clears leaves and twigs from shingles quickly, which saves hand work and gives the customer a clean roof. Use proper fall protection and work-positioning on any roof work.

A big blower is only useful if you can wear it for a full cleanup. The 590BTS uses a padded harness and back pad to spread the weight, and the throttle on the tube lets you feather airflow around flower beds, gravel, and mulch. Run lower throttle near loose stone and mulch and save full output for open pavement and lawn.
Keep the nozzle low and work in one direction, pushing debris into a pile you can rake or vacuum up instead of blowing it into a neighbor's yard.

Fit the harness before you start. Adjust the shoulder straps so the back pad sits flat and the weight rides on your hips, not your shoulders. Set the tube length so the nozzle reaches the ground comfortably without bending your wrist. These small adjustments matter more on a large, powerful blower than on a small one.

Mind noise. Many towns have rules about gas blower use and times of day. Check local ordinances, and start blowing after the saws and chipper are done so neighbors hear the noise for the shortest time possible.

Husqvarna 590BTS prices vary by dealer and region; it typically costs more than mid-range blowers such as the 580BTS. Before buying, check whether a local dealer can service it, since a commercial blower will need filters, plugs, and the occasional carburetor cleaning over its life.

Use fresh mixed fuel, clean the air filters often, and inspect the harness and tube clamps. Wear hearing and eye protection and a dust mask when blowing fine sawdust. Browse other blowers and power equipment to round out your cleanup kit.

A cleaning kit for the engine cooling fins, a spare air filter, and a spark plug on the truck will save a trip back to the shop. Inspect the harness for wear on the straps and buckles at the start of each season.
Store the blower with an empty tank or stabilized fuel if it will sit for more than a few weeks. Check the tube connections for cracks before each season.

faq.q: Is the Husqvarna 590BTS for sale as a homeowner blower?
faq.a: It can be bought by anyone, but it is a professional blower sized for commercial cleanup. Homeowners with small yards will find it more than they need.

faq.q: What fuel does the 590BTS use?
faq.a: Gasoline mixed with 2-stroke oil at the ratio in the operator's manual.

faq.q: How does it compare to a leaf blower for homeowners?
faq.a: It moves far more air and is built to be serviced and run daily, with a heavier, more comfortable harness.

name: Husqvarna K970 Power Cutter
title: Husqvarna K970 Power Cutter: Specs, Uses & Price
meta: The Husqvarna K970 is a 93.6 cc gas power cutter for concrete, stone, and steel. Blade sizes, where it helps tree crews, safety notes, and typical price.
tagline: Heavy-duty 93.6 cc gas cut-off saw for concrete, stone, and metal.
summary: The Husqvarna K970 is a heavy-duty gas power cutter with a 93.6 cc engine, built for cutting concrete, stone, asphalt, and steel. Tree and site crews reach for the K970 saw when roots run under hardscape or a removal needs a curb, slab, or pipe cut.
highlights: 93.6 cc 2-stroke engine
Takes 14 in blades, with a 16 in model available
Wet cutting kit to control dust
Active air filtration for dusty work
Built for daily commercial use

body.h: Where a power cutter fits a tree business
p: Most arborists never need a cut-off saw until the day they do. Roots heave a sidewalk and the city wants the slab cut back. A stump sits against a curb or a retaining wall. Storm cleanup leaves a steel fence or pipe tangled in a trunk. The K970 handles those jobs, cutting concrete, stone, asphalt, and steel with the right blade.
It is also a common rental-yard and contractor saw, so crews who do hardscape or site prep alongside tree work often own one.

The 93.6 cc engine gives the K970 the power to keep blade speed up in thick concrete without bogging. The standard model runs a 14 in blade, and a 16 in version gives a deeper cut. Choose a diamond blade matched to the material: a general-purpose concrete blade for slabs and curbs, an asphalt blade for paving, and an abrasive or diamond blade rated for steel when cutting metal.
Always check that the blade's maximum RPM rating is above the saw's spindle speed and that the arbor fits.

Diamond blades last much longer than abrasive wheels in concrete and stone and keep a more consistent cutting depth as they wear. Abrasive wheels still have a place for steel and occasional jobs, but wear down quickly and need to be checked for damage before every use.

Cutting concrete and stone releases respirable crystalline silica. Use the water kit for wet cutting, follow OSHA's silica rules, and wear a respirator when required. Add eye and face protection, hearing protection, gloves, and sturdy boots.

Power cutters can kick back and climb if the blade pinches or the top quadrant contacts the work. Cut with the lower part of the blade, support the work so the kerf opens rather than closes, and keep bystanders out of the spark and debris path. Read the operator's manual and get trained before running one.
Never cut with the blade above shoulder height, and do not use the K970 on a ladder. Start the saw on the ground with the blade clear, and let it reach full speed before entering the cut.

The K970 typically sells for around $1,600 to $1,700 as a bare saw, usually without a diamond blade. Budget for blades, the water kit if not included, filters, and spare plugs. Keep the air filters clean, since dust is the main enemy of a cut-off saw engine. See the rest of our power equipment for jobsite tools.
If you only need a power cutter a few times a year, renting may make more sense than owning. If your crew regularly handles root and hardscape conflicts, owning the K970 saves time and rental costs.
Write down the blade type and hours on each blade so you know when to replace it, and store blades flat in a dry place to keep them true.

faq.q: What size blade does the Husqvarna K970 take?
faq.a: The standard K970 takes a 14 in blade. A 16 in version is available for deeper cuts.

faq.q: Can the K970 saw cut roots?
faq.a: It is not designed for wood. Use a chainsaw or root saw for roots and the K970 for concrete, stone, and steel.

faq.q: Is the K970 good for wet cutting?
faq.a: Yes. Use the water kit to control silica dust when cutting concrete or stone.

name: ANSI A300 Standard for Tree Care
title: ANSI A300 Tree Care Standards: Pruning and More
h1: ANSI A300 Standard for Tree Care
meta: ANSI A300 sets the US standards for tree care operations, including pruning, support systems, and soil work. What each part covers and who needs it.
tagline: The US consensus standard for how tree care work should be done.
summary: ANSI A300 is the American National Standard for tree care operations, covering how pruning, cabling, soil management, and other work should be specified and done. Arborists, municipalities, and consultants use the ANSI A300 pruning standards and other parts to write specs and set expectations with clients.
highlights: Written by an accredited consensus committee
Covers pruning, support systems, soil, and more
Basis for professional tree care specifications
Useful for ISA certification study
Compact reference for the truck or office

p: ANSI A300 is published in parts. Part 1 covers pruning, and other parts address soil management, supplemental support systems such as cabling and bracing, lightning protection, construction management, planting, root management, and tree risk assessment. Together they describe what good tree care looks like and the terms used to specify it.
Many people search for ANSI 300 or A300 pruning standards; both refer to this set of documents. ISA publishes companion Best Management Practices that explain how to apply each part.

The standards are written to be referenced in contracts. A spec can say, for example, that pruning will be performed according to ANSI A300 Part 1, with the objective and cut types listed. That gives you and the client a shared language for what is being done.

If you write work orders, bid municipal or utility contracts, or prepare for the ISA Certified Arborist exam, keep the relevant parts on hand. Quoting the standard in a proposal helps clients understand why you prune the way you do. For the safety side of the job, pair it with the ANSI Z133 safety standard.
Arborists preparing for the ISA exam will find that many questions draw on A300 pruning terms and objectives, so reading the standard alongside the study guide is time well spent.

faq.q: Is ANSI A300 the same as Z133?
faq.a: No. A300 covers how tree care work is done and specified; Z133 covers safety requirements for arboricultural operations.

faq.q: Do I need every part?
faq.a: Most arborists start with Part 1 (Pruning) and add others that match their services.

name: ANSI Z133 Safety Standard for Arboricultural Operations
title: ANSI Z133 Safety Standard for Tree Work
h1: ANSI Z133 Safety Standard for Tree Work
meta: ANSI Z133 is the US safety standard for arboricultural operations: climbing, rigging, saws, electrical hazards, and PPE. What's in it and who needs it.
tagline: The safety standard every tree care crew should keep on the truck.
summary: ANSI Z133 is the American National Standard for safety requirements in arboricultural operations. It covers climbing, rigging, chainsaw use, electrical hazards, traffic control, and personal protective equipment for tree workers.
highlights: The core safety standard for US tree work
Covers climbing, rigging, saws, and equipment
Electrical hazard and minimum approach distances
PPE requirements for crews
Used by employers, trainers, and inspectors

p: Z133 sets minimum safety requirements for tree work. It covers general safety and job briefings, electrical hazards and approach distances, vehicles and mobile equipment, portable power tools and chainsaws, hand tools, work-positioning and fall protection for climbers, rigging, felling, and PPE. People also search for it as Z133 or anzi z133; it is the same standard.
Many employers and insurers treat Z133 as the baseline for how their crews work, and OSHA may reference it in enforcement.
It also covers job briefings, work zones and traffic control, chippers and stump grinders, aerial lifts, cranes, and emergency response, which makes it useful for ground crews as well as climbers.

Keep a copy on each truck and use it in tailgate meetings. Go through the climbing and rigging sections with new hires, and refer to it when you choose gear such as ascent and descent devices. Reading the standard does not replace hands-on training; pair it with qualified instruction. For tree care practices, see ANSI A300.
Many crews mark up a copy with tabs for the sections they reference most, such as approach distances and rigging, so answers are easy to find during a job briefing.
New climbers should read the climbing and rigging sections early, and crew leaders should revisit the electrical section often.

faq.q: Is ANSI Z133 required by law?
faq.a: It is a voluntary consensus standard, but employers, contracts, and regulators commonly reference it as the expected practice.

faq.q: How often is Z133 updated?
faq.a: It is revised periodically. Make sure you have the current edition.

name: ISA Arborists' Certification Study Guide
title: ISA Arborist Study Guide for Certification
h1: ISA Arborist Study Guide for Certification
